name: Ashkenaz
overview: Ashkenaz is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Gomer, as recorded in Genesis 10:3. Beyond this genealogical detail, there is no additional information about his tribe or other attributes. His mention situates him within the post-Flood genealogical framework that traces the origins of various peoples.
namesAndTitles: The name Ashkenaz appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:3. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to this name in the biblical text, and thus it is presented plainly without additional significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ashkenaz as a son of Gomer, establishing a direct father-son relationship. No further family connections or descendants are mentioned in the biblical record beyond this relationship.
scriptureSignificance: Ashkenaz's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical listings of Genesis, which outline the descendants of Noah's son Japheth through Gomer. His mention helps frame the understanding of the dispersion and origins of nations after the Flood, contributing to the biblical narrative of God's providential ordering of peoples.
